one_liner: Vercel has a REST API at api.vercel.com with self-serve account access tokens and integration OAuth-style code exchange. A toolkit looks buildable now. The fetched pages don't confirm the MCP server or the free-plan claim.
auth_notes: Access tokens are created in account settings and sent as a Bearer header. Integrations get a REST API access token by exchanging a code at their Redirect URL, which is an OAuth-style flow. Scopes are set per integration. The pages don't give the OAuth endpoints, so access tokens are the fallback.
access_notes: The pages show that tokens are created in account settings. They don't state which plan is needed. The free Hobby plan claim came from a pricing page that isn't among the fetched pages, so treat this as likely but unverified.
blocker_notes: No blocker is visible in the fetched pages. The MCP server's official status could not be checked against these pages. It rests on the draft, the Composio catalog entry "Vercel MCP" and the vendor URL, so confidence is low. Plan requirements are also not stated on the fetched pages.

evidence.quote: Vercel Access Tokens are required to authenticate and use the Vercel API.
Create and manage Access Tokens in your [account settings](https://vercel.com/account/tokens).
Token Exchange: Exchanges a provided code for a [Vercel REST API access token]
All endpoints live under the URL `https://api.vercel.com` and follow the REST architecture.
With your integration, you can listen for events on the Vercel platform through Webhooks.
